dedupe_keys.name: emergency evacuation challenges for residents near a refinery after an earthquake triggered h2s release natech scenario tehran 2022

description: This case study examines the challenges of evacuating residential areas next to a refinery near Tehran if an earthquake damaged the plant and released hydrogen sulphide, a Natech event in which a natural hazard triggers a technological accident. In a first phase the authors reviewed past community experience of evacuation after Natech events; in a second phase they analysed evacuation for a possible earthquake scenario with a gas release. Because buildings in the area are highly vulnerable to earthquakes, the whole resident population would be hit by the earthquake and by H2S at 30 ppm at the same time, so evacuation would be unavoidable; the existing evacuation places were found unsafe, and the nearest suitable ones lay to the north for more than 38% of the exposed population and to the east, west and south for more than 61%. It was carried out in 2020 by Parvin Shafiei Moghaddam and co-authors and published in the Journal of Injury and Violence Research in January 2022. The article is available free online under CC BY 3.0. Caveats: the refinery is not named and the analysis rests on one scenario. For simulation it gives the evacuation side of an earthquake to toxic release chain, useful for Natech scenarios that link seismic damage, gas dispersion and shelter capacity. It is related to the refinery H2S Natech risk assessment record in this catalogue by the same research group.
